title: How is the "Userpaused" state recognized?
body:
The paper mentions: When the VAD detects active speech, the system transitions to the UserSpeaking state. During this state, the Streaming Audio Tokenizer begins converting audio into tokens. If the user momentarily pauses, the system enters the UserPaused state, where speculative response generation is triggered. By preemptively generating a response in anticipation of input completion, the system reduces latency when the conversation resumes. If the user resumes speaking, the speculative response is discarded. Once the system confidently determines that the user has finished speaking, it transitions to the BotReplying state, commits the most recent speculative response, and delivers its audio output.

How are the states of "Userpaused" and "BotReplying" identified? The recognition of the "BotReplying" state is an existing capability of VAD (for example, if the user has not spoken for 500ms). How is the "Userpaused" state recognized?

Thanks!
author: forest520

comments.body:
I have the same question. I've been looking into full-duplex interaction mechanisms and state transitions lately. 

My guess is that it might be managed by a VAD threshold—say, if there's more than 250ms of silence, it’s treated as a user pause. But hey, that's just my speculation; I'm waiting for the official word.

> I have the same question. I've been looking into full-duplex interaction mechanisms and state transitions lately.
> 
> My guess is that it might be managed by a VAD threshold—say, if there's more than 250ms of silence, it’s treated as a user pause. But hey, that's just my speculation; I'm waiting for the official word.

The paper states: "This mechanism reduces per-response latency by approximately 500ms compared to non-speculative methods."

If the UserPaused state represents a user pause of 250ms without speech, and assuming the VAD silence duration normally requires 500ms to trigger the BotReplying state, then the speculative mechanism would only save 500-250=250ms in this scenario, not the 500ms claimed in the paper. What are your thoughts on this discrepancy?

The `UserPaused` state is managed by two different VAD thresholds. For our testing we chose silent duration of 250ms and 750ms for `UserPaused` and `BotReplying`. However, depending on your specific use case, other parameter values may be more suitable.

title: Inquiry Regarding End-to-End Audio Output Architecture
body:
Dear Step-Audio Team,

First and foremost, I would like to extend my sincere appreciation for your team's groundbreaking achievements in this field.

While reviewing your technical proposal, I observed that, as an innovative multimodal architecture, the speech processing module employs a front-end encoder to directly generate discrete representation units (tokens). Given that the current technical approach relies on CosyVoice for waveform reconstruction in system outputs, I am curious whether your technical roadmap has contemplated constructing an end-to-end audio output architecture independent of CosyVoice.

I would greatly value your professional insights regarding the feasibility of direct continuous audio stream generation and any potential technical challenges involved.

Keep up the amazing work, and thank you for your contributions to the field!

Looking forward to hearing from you!

Best regards.
author: vonchenplus

comments.body:
Step-Audio's design is not tied to CosyVoice, but still tied to audio tokenizer. The input would be inflated to 100x larger if bytes from a wav file is directly used.
Nevertheless, our key takeaway from Step-Audio is that auto-regression is key to modeling of audio. As long as AR is there, other ways of using continuous/discrete representation is quite possible.
